key_insight: EmoRES-TTS improves emotion control in text-to-speech without retraining the model by steering internal representations more effectively. It refines conventional vector steering so emotional speech is expressed more reliably and with less computational cost.
problem_solved: Emotion-conditioned TTS models often fail to consistently produce the requested emotion, and improving this usually requires expensive retraining and emotion-labeled speech data. This paper addresses the need for a training-free, lower-cost way to better control emotional expression in frozen TTS models.
method: Uses training-free vector steering to adjust hidden representations inside a frozen emotion TTS model.
Introduces residual-enhanced steering, which likely decomposes or refines emotion directions beyond a single global vector to improve controllability.
Builds on conventional methods like CoCoEmo to make emotion control more precise and robust without additional model training.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to improve emotional speech generation without expensive fine-tuning or new labeled data. It is especially useful for deploying controllable TTS systems more efficiently and flexibly.
visual_elements: Before/after waveform or spectrogram comparison showing neutral vs emotional speech
Pipeline diagram of frozen TTS model with vector steering inserted into internal representations
Side-by-side comparison of CoCoEmo vs EmoRES-TTS steering mechanisms

paper_title: EmoRES-TTS: Residual-Enhanced Vector Steering for Emotional Speech Generation
paper_authors: Kuan-Po Huang, Haohe Liu, Puyuan Peng, Haibin Wu, Zhaoheng Ni
